latin.note: ANTECEDENT, NOT THE CONTROLLING EDITION. The Latin here is the facing column of the 1861 Philadelphia Cummiskey hand missal at its In spiritu humilitatis, printed page xxiv, Internet Archive leaf 34. The Latin of the Missale Romanum, editio typica tertia 2002 with its emended reprint of 2008 is not served here. The repository holds and has read a verified 2002 Ordo witness and the official bounded 2008 variation list, but that evidence does not establish this word identity; these are the 1861 printing's words. THE WITNESS MISPRINTS nodie FOR hodie, and it is carried as printed and not corrected: the letter is an n, with no ascender, read at 200 per cent magnification against the h of hoc on the same page and recorded in the artifact's own transcriber's note. It is that printer's error. Nothing here attributes it to the Missal, and correcting it silently would have manufactured a target witness this project has not established. The visually checked 1862 Pustet page at passage.catholic-church.missale-romanum.pustet-ratisbon-1862.ordo-missae-leaf-303 prints hodie and confirms only that the 1861 n is not the older prayer's general reading; it does not establish the postconciliar target. UNCOLLATED: the identity of this text with the controlling edition's is not established here. This repository's study of this Order of Mass states at n. 26, in 00-order-of-mass/sections/40-preparation-of-the-gifts.tex:108-110, that the prayer is taken from the Song of the Three Young Men and is retained from the older Order, and it quotes the 2002 Latin of the opening clause only, as far as suscipiamur a te, Domine. That clause and this witness agree word for word. The rest of the prayer, the misprint among it, has not been compared with anything.

latin.reading_note: Latin from Pustet (1862), collated word for word to the complete prayer expressly cited from the 2008 Missal in Desiderio desideravi. Source punctuation is retained; this is not a complete liturgical edition.
latin.note: The Latin is independently transcribed from Pustet, Ratisbon 1862, printed p.218 / complete PDF p.304 / IA n303. It reads hodie and contains no Amen. Stress accents are removed, physical wrapping joined and initial small capitals rendered in sentence case; all source words, word order and punctuation remain. The whole prayer agrees word for word, apart from those display conventions and punctuation, with the official Latin Desiderio desideravi 60 quotation, Notitiae 2022 printed p.53 / PDF p.55, note 20 expressly citing Missale Romanum (2008), p.515. The comparison establishes this one complete prayer’s wording, not a complete 2008 exemplar, modern rubrics, chant, liturgical approval or approved English. Cummiskey 1861 remains a separate source: its literal nodie is preserved in its original artifact and in the prior source-selection receipt; no Cummiskey byte is repaired or attributed to Pustet. Historical English retains its existing, independently identified Cummiskey witness and its own uncollated status.

whole_expression_publication_assessment.source_extent: One whole, uninterrupted prayer printed in 1862; no composed joins or changed words.
whole_expression_publication_assessment.priority: Independent historical public-domain expression under publication policy priorities 1 and 3; 17 USC 103(b) confines later derivative copyright to new authorship.
whole_expression_publication_assessment.reasoning: The entire petition, its order and its ending already occur together in the independently held 1862 printing. There is no newly composed petition, expressive alteration, recombination, addition, omission, or conclusion expansion. The modern quotation supplies comparison only. Pointing, capitalization, accents and wrapping do not supply an independent newly authored prayer expression. No exclusive modern page arrangement, annotation, typography, chant or rubrics are copied.
whole_expression_publication_assessment.strongest_adverse_case: The modern Missal and the official letter/journal retain distinct rights and the official quotation alone is neither a reproduction license nor the actual Missal page. These limits prevent whole-edition clearance and claims about surrounding execution. They do not change the independently demonstrated historical identity of this one complete prayer.
whole_expression_publication_assessment.confidence: high; finite to this prayer; awaits independent acceptance

comparison_method: Fresh direct images of Pustet 1862 AP304 and Notitiae2022 AP55. Complete prayer words and order compared. Only accents, capitals, punctuation and physical wrapping ignored for word-exactness; selected artifact retains Pustet punctuation. The official Latin quote explicitly identifies 2008 Missale p.515 in note20.

prose_replacements.and every one of them is carried as prin: and every one remains in that source artifact. The In spiritu humilitatis selection now names the independently collated 1862 Pustet source; no 1861 artifact byte is repaired.
prose_replacements.and nodie for hodie at In spiritu humili: and nodie for hodie in its In spiritu humilitatis row are the 1861 printer's and not the Holy See's. That row remains in the source artifact; the current selection of this prayer independently names Pustet 1862.
